prop_correlation.why: No historical player-prop line archive is reachable from this environment. Prop-to-prop correlations therefore cannot be measured from outcomes, and no number is published rather than an estimate.
what_would_fix_it: A licensed prop-line history (e.g. a sportsbook API or a paid odds archive) for at least three seasons, with closing prices.
Player-week box scores joined by game id, so each prop can be settled.
Enough same-game prop pairs to estimate a phi coefficient per pair.

structural_relationships_only.reason: the same completions produce both; a parlay of the two is one bet on the passing game, not two independent bets.
a touchdown pass is the receiving touchdown; the two legs are almost the same event.
a run-heavy game script raises both.
run-heavy and pass-heavy game scripts trade off against each other.
winning teams run more plays and keep the ball.
a higher-scoring game is usually a higher-volume passing game.
sacks end drives and suppress passing volume.
field goals replace touchdowns in low-scoring games.

team_score_correlation.interpretation: Scores are close to uncorrelated, so opposing team-total overs are closer to independent than the pace story implies.

slate.source: DraftKings main-slate salary export, Week 9 2026 (11/08/2026), mirrored in-repo at pipeline/data/raw/dfs/
slate.note_on_status: IR / OUT / Q / D flags are the book's own availability markers on this export. They are not the NFL's official designations and must be cross-checked against the official injury report before use.

recommendation: Until prop history exists, price player-prop combos with the structural sign map plus a wide safety margin, and treat the game-level correlations in correlation.json as the only verified correlation inputs.
